OBITUARY RE FERENCES  
MR. CHAIRMAN: Honourable Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing away of Shri 
Swapnananda Panigrahi and Shri Balbir Singh, former Members of this House. 
Shri Swapnananda Panigrahi, passed away on the 7th November, 2007 at the age of 85 years. 
Born at Degaon of Patna State in November, 1923, Shri Panigrahi had his education  at Bolangir and 
Cuttack. 
A lawyer, Shri Panigrahi plunged into political activities right from his student days. He organised political 
and student movements for the merger of Patna and neighboring States in 1946-47. He also worked for 
the abolition of untouchability. 
Shri Panigrahi represented the State of Orissa in this House from April, 1954 to Aprl, 1960. 
In the passing away of Shri Swapnananda Panigrahi, the country has lost a noted social 
worker. 
Shri Balbir Singh passed away on the 13th February, 2008 at the age of 70 years. 
Born at Shanker in the Jalandhar District of Punjab in December, 1938, Shri Singh had his education at the 
Punjab University, Chandigarh; Indian Institute of Public Administration , New Delhi; IIM, Ahmedabad and 
National Productivity Council, Mumbai. 
An advocate by profession, Shri Singh was associated with various social welfare and educational 
institutions. He was President of the Governing Council of Lyallpur Khalsa College for Boys and Girls. He 
worked for the welfare of immigrants settled in the UK, the USA and Canada. Shri Singh was a keen sports 
lover, especially Kabaddi. He also served in various capacities in different sports associations. 
Shri Singh began his legislative career as a Member of Punjab Legislative Assembly where he was a 
Member from 1972 to 1977. He also served as Minister of State (Independent Charge) in the Punjab Government 
during the period 1973 to 1977. 
Shri Singh represented the State of Punjab in this House from April 1992 to April, 1998. was also a 
Member of the 13th Lok Sabha. 
 the passing away of Shri Balbir Singh, the country has lost an able parliamentarian  a true sports 
lover.

Sethusamudram Canal  
*41. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether according to the book entitled "Images India" published by NRSA (National Remote 
Sensing Agency), satellite images have revealed tha t "an ancient bridge existed between India and 
Sri Lanka in Palk Strait"; 
(b)  if so, whether Government is also aware that a large number of people in the country consider 
Ram Setu/Adams Bridge, a national monument due to i ts antiquity and unique features/historical 
importance in Ram Charit Manas; and 
(c)  if so, Government's final decision regarding construction of Sethusamudram Canal by dredging a 
portion of Ram Setu and whether the same has been conveyed to the Supreme Court? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. BAALU): (a) 
In the brief note given in the atlas for the image showing Adam's Bridge in the publication 'Images India' 
brought out in 2006 by National Remote Sensing Agency (NRSA) of the Department of Space, it has, inter 
alia, been stated that satellite images have revealed an ancient bridge between India and Sri Lanka in the 
Palk Strait. It is also states that it is made of a  chain of shoals. The Atlas/Book on 'Images India' brought 
out in 2006 by National * Remote Sensing Agency (NRSA) is basically a compendium of satellite images 
taken from Indian Remote Sensing Satellites (IRS) e ssentially intended for creating public awareness o n 
the diverse landscapes of the country, and to popularize the use of space images. 
(b) and (c) The Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project,  which was approved by the Government 
in May, 2005, involves dredging for the creation of a continuous navigational channel connecting the 
Gulf of Mannar and the Bay of Bengal through Adam's Bridge, Palk Bay and Palk Strait with a view to 
providing a continuous navigable route connecting the east and west coasts and running within its own 
territorial waters around the Indian Peninsula. However, pursuant to orders passed by the Supreme 
Court on 31.8.2007 and 14.9.2007, dredging work at Adam's Bridge area has been suspended. 
Further, pursuant to the submissions made before th e Hon'ble Supreme Court of India by the 
Government Counsel

Preparations for Beijing Olympics  
*42. SHRIS. ANBALAGAN: Will  the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be     , pleased to 
state: 
(a) the preparations made for winning more medals in the forthcoming Beijing Olympics; 
(b)  whether any steps have been taken to sort out the p roblems being faced by our    * athletes and 
sportspersons which prevent them from winning medal s at Olympic Games even though we are the 
second largest country in the world; 
(c)  if so, the specific steps taken by Government durin g each of the last three years in this 
regard and the sports and events in which our sport spersons are expected to excel during the 
forthcoming Olympic games; and 
(d)  the amount spent by the Union Government on preparations for Olympics, so far? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTHAFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI SHANKARAIYAR): (a) As 
against one silver medal won in Athens Olympics 200 4, the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and the 
National Sports Federations (NSFs) have identified medal probables in 6 of the 11 disciplines in 
which India is likely to participate in Beijing Oly mpic, 2008 and are implementing their training 
programme in terms of coaching, international expos ures, scientific and equipment support and 
engagement of foreign coaches. On the basis of the training given and the current performances of 
the players, India is estimated to hold promising m edal prospects in the disciplines of Shooting, 
Archery, Wrestling, Boxing, Athletics and Tennis. 
(b)  While the steps outlined in (a) above are designed to overcome specific problems in different 
prospective sports disciplines, our overall perform ance in the Olympics has not been satisfactory in t he 
past mainly because of the narrow pool of talented athletes from which our talent is drawn compared to  
the overall strength of our youth population. Talen t on a vast scale has to be spotted, nurtured and 
trained to eventually and exponentially expand our medal prospects. With a view to addressing this 
issue, the Ministry proposes to implement Panchayat  Yuva Krida Aur Khel Abhiyan, which is aimed at 
providing basic sports infrastructure and promoting  sports competitions at the grassroots level. Apart  
from broad-basing of sports, in the long run, this will result in exponential growth in the identification of 
gifted and talented athletes who can then be groome d in to high performing athletes and thus lead to 
increased medal prospects at the international leve l. The Ministry has also prepared a Draft 
Comprehensive National Sports Policy, 2008, which a part from addressing the deficiencies in the 
system, aims at generating a positive attitude towa rds sports in the country thus facilitating the 
emergence of India as a leading sporting nation. 
(c)  and (d) Preparations for winning more medals in all  major international events, including 
the Beijing Olympics, is an on-going process and is  based on the Long Term Development Plans 
(LTDP) prepared by the NSFs. Government provides assistance to the

Software for registered farmers 
*44. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether IIT, Bombay has developed a software with which registered farmers can have their queries 
answered on a mobile phone without having to go to a kiosk or cyber cafe; 
(b)  if so, will farmers from Vidarbha region be made familiar with such a cost-effective mechanism through 
which they get answers to their agriculture and animal husbandry related questions; and 
(c)  the cost involved and the time-frame for starting the functioning of this software from Vidarbha? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to 
(c) Yes, Sir. IIT, Bombay has developed Software AAQUA (Almost All Questions Answered) under a project 
undertaken at a cost of Rs. 1.62 crore out of which Department of Information Technology (DIT) funding was 
provided to an extent of Rs. 87 lakhs through Media Lab Asia. With the help of this software, rural users can 
have their queries/problems addressed by the experts. Interactions between users and experts happen via the web 
portal (www.aaqua.org ) and SMS. The AAQUA site has already been responding to queries from users, including 
from Vidarbha. As of now, queries are answered primarily by experts from Krishi Vigyan Kendra, 
Baramati.

Completion of EW and NS Corridors 
*46. MS. MABEL REBELLO:  Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
be pleased to state: 
(a)  by when the East-West and North-South corridors of the National Highways would be completed; 
(b)  the distance in kilometres that needs to be completed; and 
(c)  the problems being faced in its completion? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. B AALU):  (a) 
Four laning of the East-West and North-South (EW-NS) corridor is likely to be substantially completed by 2009 
excepting for a few projects which may be completed by 2010. 
(b)  An aggregate length of 5,473 km remains to be completed, out of which work is already in progress in 
4,652 km. The balance for award of contract is 821 km. 
(c)  The main problems being faced relate to land acquis ition, shifting of religious structures and 
graveyards approval of designs of Road Over Bridges  (ROBs), law and order, realignment of some stretch es, 
slow progress by some contractors and delay in obtaining forest clearance for some stretches. 
Extraction of dolomite from Bhutan  
*47. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY:  Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to refer to the  answer to 
Unstarred Question 467 given in the Rajya Sabha on 22nd November, 2007 and state: 
(a)  when was the Joint Technical Team constituted; and 
(b)  the action taken on the recommendation of the Joint Technical Team so far? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI NAMO 
NARAIN MEENA):  (a) A Joint Group of Experts (JGE) on Flood Management was constituted between India 
and Bhutan to discuss and assess the probable cause s and effects of the recurring floods and erosion i n the 
southern foothills of Bhutan and adjoining plains in India and to recommend appropriate and mutually acceptable 
remedial measures to both the Governments. 
The first meeting of JGE was held in Bhutan from 1st to 5th November, 2004 and inter-alia a Joint Technical 
Team (JTT) was set up. JTT was entrusted with the tasks of assessment of the problems of flood and landslides 
and suggest remedial measures with respect to rivers flowing from Bhutan. 
(b) The JTT has finalized and submitted its prelimi nary report during January 2006. In the report, JTT  
recommended taking up further studies on the subject. The second meeting of the JGE was scheduled for 26-
27th February, 2008 at New Delhi. 
Shift in flow of Ganga river 
*48. SHRI ABU AS1M AZMI: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that due to wrost environmental conditions on the Gangotri glacier 

10    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Starred Questions  
in the Himalaya Mountain, the flow of river Ganga h as gone far away from the main source 
'Gaumukh'; 
(b)  if so, whether any survey has been conducted in this regard; 
(c)  if so, the details and the outcome thereof; and 
(d)  The steps taken/being taken by the Government to br ing back the flow of river Ganga to 
'Gaumukh'? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMEN T AND FORESTS 
(SHRINAMO NARAIN MEENA):  (a) to (d) The river Ganga originates from 'Gaumuk' which is the 
mouth of the Gangotri glacier. The Geological Survey of India (GSI) has been carrying out studies on the 
recession of Gangotri glacier since 1935. As per data available with GSI, Gangotri glacier has receded 
by 18.80 metres (m)/year during 1935—96 period. The Gangotri glacier showed a higher rate of recession 
between 1956 and 1996. The highest rate of recession in the order of 38.00m/year was recorded during 
1975-76. GSI has not carried out studies on recession of Gangotri glacier since 1996. Studies by other 
organizations after 1996 have revealed a rate of 12.10 m/year during 2004-05. As far as recession of the 
glaciers is concerned, it is a natural phenomenon a nd cannot be stopped using short term artificial 
measures.

Arresting migration to urban areas  
*59. KUMARI.NIRMALA DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of  HOUSING AND URBAN 
POVERTY ALLEVIATION  be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether there is any policy to make life in rural a reas livable and also provide employment 
there, so that the inflow to urban area as is arrested; and 
(b)  if not, the other measures undertaken to help the urban poor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA):  (a) The Government of India has adopted a two pron ged 
approach for tackling rural poverty in the country: firstly by providing basic amenities in rural areas 
through schemes like Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yoja na (PMGSY), Bharat Nirman, Accelerated 
Rural Water Supply Programme, National Rural Health Mission, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and Mid Day 
Meal (MDM) Scheme; and secondly by targeted employment generation schemes like Swarna Jayanti 
Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY), and the National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS). 
(b) In the urban areas, the Government is implementing the Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana 
(SJSRY) for addressing the income generation/liveli hood needs of the urban poor living below the 
poverty line. The scheme of Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) strives to provide gainful 
employment to the urban unemployed and underemployed poor by firstly, encouraging the setting up 
of self-employment ventures by those who have not s tudied beyond 9th standard and, secondly, by 
providing wage employment for construction of socia lly and economically useful public assets.

Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM). The sub-Mission of Basic Service 
for Urban Poor (BSUP) under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) caters to 
63 identified Cities and Integrated Housing and Slum Development Programme (IHSDP) applies to cities/ 
towns other than the 63 identified cities. The Jawa harlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission 
(JNNURM) stipulates and provision of education, health and social security benefits to the urban poor 
through convergence of all relevant programmes of the Central and State Governments at the urban 
local body level.

Deliberations on climate changes  
221.   SHRI O.T.LEPCHA: 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether Government has taken an account of the gains and losses-liabilities arising out of the 
deliberations on climate changes lately held at Bali talks to contain and prevent the adverse effects of 
climate change; 
(b)  if so, the advantages and gains that have been secured at the talks for the developing nations and the 
assurances given by the developed industrialized nations for development of the developing countries; and 
(c)  the losses and liabilities that have been incurred by the developing nations as a result of the Bali talks? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI NAMO 
NARAIN MEENA): (a) to (c) The thirteenth Conference of Parties (COP-13) to the United Nations Framework 
Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the third Meeting of parties (MOP-3) to Kyoto Protocol was 
held in Bali in December 2007. The principal outcome of the Bali conference was to launch a comprehensive 
process called Bali Action Plan (BAP) that would enable the full, effective and sustained implementation of the 
UNFCCC through long-term cooperative action, now up to and beyond 2012. It is expected that an agreed outcome 
would be reached and a decision adopted regarding BAP, at the fifteenth Conference of Parties (COP-15) to be 
held in December 2009. 
The Conference of Parties serving as meeting of Parties at Bali also took crucial decisions in respect of 
the Kyoto Protocol, the Ad-hoc Working Group on further commitments of developed countries (beyond 
2012) finally established a deadline of 2009 for the completion of its work and forwarding to COP-15 for 
a decision, its recommendations on quantified emissions limitation and reduction commitments of Annex I 
Parties (developed countries). 
Several other significant decisions which are beneficial to developing countries were also reached at Bali. 
These include operationalization of the Adaptation Fund to provide assistance to developing countries to adapt to 
climate change; agreement on guidance for the further implementation and improvement of the Clean 
Development Mechanism; policy approaches and positive incentives on issues relating to reducing 
emissions from deforestation and forest degradation in developing countries and the role of conservation, 
sustainable management of forests and enhancement of forest carbon stocks in developing countries, "transfer of 
technologies", including licenses to support the access to and transfer of low carbon technologies, an d 
know-how. 
It is expected that the decisions taken at Bali would enhance the implementation of the UNFCCC and 
as a responsible country, India will engage constructively in these negotiations.

227. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI 
NAMONARA1N MEENA): (a) and (b) Even though India as a developing country does not have any 
mitigation commitments, nevertheless, a sustainable development path is being followed through a 
range of policies and programmes to mitigate climate change and reduce carbon emissions. Some of 
the steps taken by the Government, include inter alia:  
(i) Setting up of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency a nd encouraging energy conservation and 
introduction of energy efficiency labeling. 
(ii)  promoting use of renewable energy. 
(iii)  power sector reforms and active renewable energy programme. 
(iv)  use of cleaner and lesser carbon intensive fuel for transport. 
(v)  fuel switching to cleaner energy. 
(vi)  afforestation and conservation of forests 
(vii)  promotion of clean coal technologies. 
(viii)  reduction of gas flaring. 
(ix)  Encouraging Mass Rapid Transport systems. 
 (x)  environment quality management for all sectors. 
The National Environment Policy 2006 of Ministry of Environment & Forests inter alia addresses 
the issue of global warming. The following comprise essential elements of India's response to climate 
change. 
(a) Adherence to the principle common but different iated responsibilities and respective 
capabilities of different countries in respect of b oth mitigation of Green House Gases 
(GHGs). and adaptation measures

(b)  Reliance on multilateral approaches, as opposed to bilateral or plurilateral or unilateral 
measures. 
(c)  Equal per-capita entitlements of global environmental resources to all countries. 
(d)  Over-riding priority of the right to development. 
(e)  Identify key vulnerabilities of India to climate change, inparticular impacts on water resources, 
forests, coastal areas, agriculture, and health. 
(f)  Assess the need for adaptation to future climate change, and the scope for incorporating these 
in relevant programmes, including watershed managem ent, coastal zone planning and 
regulation, forestry management, agricultural techn ologies and practices, and health 
programmes. 
(g)  Encourage Indian Industry to participate in the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) through 
capacity building for identifying and preparing CDM projects, including the financial sector. 
(h) Participate in voluntary partnerships with other countries both developed and developing to address 
the challengers of sustainable development and climate change, consistent with the provisions of 
the UN Framework convention on Climate Change. 
Further, the Government has also set up "Expert Committee on Impacts of Climate Change" in May 2007 to 
study the impacts of anthropogenic climate change on India and to identify the measures that we may have to 
take in the future in relation to addressing vulnerability to anthropogenic climate change impacts. 
A coordination committee chaired by Hon'ble Prime Minister called "Prime Minister's council on climate 
Change to coordinate national action for assessment, adaptation and mitigation of climate change" was 
constituted on 6th June 2007. The focus of the Committee would be to:

(c)  how far it has adversely effected the fertility of agricultural land, water resources and breathing

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI 
NAMO N ARAIN MEENA): (a) and (b) Surface air temperatures over the India for the period 1901-2000 
indicate a significant warming of about 0.5°C/100 y ear during the last century. The ten warmest 
years on record are 2006(0.595), 2002(0.59), 1998(0 .50), 2004 & 2001(0.47),2003(0.45), 1958(0.43),

are the differences from the long term mean. Since 1993, annual mean temperature has been 
consistently above normal. The year 2006 was the wa rmest year on record since 1901. The year 
2001 was warmer by 0.55°C. The assessment for the y ear 2008 will be available only by the end of 
the year. The spatial distribution of temperature c hanges indicate that a significant warming trend 
has been observed along the west coast, central Ind ia, and interior Peninsula and over northeast 
India. However, cooling trend has been observed in northwest and some parts in southern India. 
These observed trends are based on Instrumental rec ords over the past more than 100 years, 
collected by the India Meteorological Department.

environmentally unsound recycling practices have the potential to cause adverse impacts on environment and 
health. 
The Government of India has notified the Plastics Manufacture Sale and Usage Rules, 1999 amended 2003 
under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. As per these rules, manufacture, stocking distribution, or selling 
of carry bags made of virgin or recycled plastic which are less than 20 x 30 cms in size and 20 microns thickness 
is banned. These rules also prohibit use of recycled plastic bags and containers for storing, carrying , 
dispensing or packaging of foodstuffs. Further, units manufacturing carry bags or containers made of virgin and 
recycled plastics are required to register with the concerned State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) or 
Pollution Control Committee (PCC) prior to the commencement of production. 
As per information made available by State Pollution Control Boards, the States like Maharashtra, Punjab, 
Chandigarh, Kerala, Meghalaya and Goa have laid down stricter norms than prescribed with regard to thickness of 
plastic bags viz. 50,30,30,30,40 and 40 microns respectively. The State of Himachal Pradesh has banned carrry 
bags made of non biodegradable material of thickness less than 70 microns and size less than 18x12 inches. The 
Government of West Bengal has banned the manufacture, use, storage and sale of plastic carry bags of thickness 
below 40 microns and of size 16 x 12". Further the States of Gujarat, Orissa and Goa has banned use of plastic 
bags in certain religious and tourist places like Ambaji, Dakor, Somnath in Gujarat and municipal area of Puri and 
Konark in Orissa. The concerned State Governments and the Union Territory Administrations are monitoring 
the implementation.

well within prescribe ambient air quality standards in Delhi.

* Strengthening 'Pollution Under Control (PUC)' Certificate system for in-use vehicles. 
* Introduction of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), a cleaner fuel for public transport to replace

(c)  to (d) Yes. The manuscripts are _atalogued and preserved in the Bhandarkar Oriental Research 
Institute, Pune. 
There are 30 manuscripts. All the manuscrips are Sanskrit language. One manuscript is written on 
birch bark in the ancient Sharada script. The remaining 29 manuscrips are written on paper in the 
Devangari script. The oldest manuscript is no. 5/1882-83 and is dated 1464 A.D. These manuscripts 
have several unique features in terms of scripts, a ccentuation marks and support material used. These 
manuscripts are valuable as unique examples of the intellectual and cultural heritage not only of India, 
but of the world. The IndoLogist, Prof. F. Max Muller, used of these Rigveda manuscripts to prepare his 
critical edition of the Rigveda. The material in this collection of Rigveda manuscripts was also used 
to prepare the well-known Critical Edition of the Rigveda by the Vaidika Samshodhana Mandala, a 
premier institute in Pune for Vedic Studies. 
The National Mission for Manuscripts launched to preserve the heritage and culture of India, has 
set up a Manuscript Conservation Centre at this Ins titute for providing support in manuscript 
conservation. The manuscripts are given preventive conservation treatment by way of dusting, 
cleaming and airing. They are kept in good climatic  conditions. Handling of the manuscripts is 
restricted. 
All the manuscripts are kept in cupboards of well-s easoned Burma teakwood placed in the 
Manuscripts Hall of the Institute. The edges of the  birch bark manuscript are lined with paper and 
sheets of soft and this tissue paper have been inserted between every two folios. It is placed in a hard 
cardboard box lined with Rexene. This box is placed  carefully in a wooden drawer of a wooden 
cupboard meant for the manuscript. The other manusc ripts, written on paper, are supported with hard 
carboards on both sides, wrapped in red cloth and a re placed in the Burma teak cupboards of the 
Manuscripts Library.

Rising  land and flat prices  
269. SHR1 S. ANBALAGAN: Will the Minister of  HOUSI NG AND URBAN POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether Government is aware that purchasing or constructing a new house/flat has becoming 
a distant dream for millions of lower and middle class people due to sky rocketing of land and flat 
prices in urban areas of the country during the last three years; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof, particularly for the me tros (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata) 
with percentage of increase in market price of land and flats during the period; and 
(c)  the steps proposed to be taken by the Union Governm ent to deal with the situation so as to 
facilitate the lower and middle class people's dream of owning their own house/flat? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AN D URBAN POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) to (c) The Ministry is concerned about affordability of houses 
for different sections of society. 
In order to address the issue of affordability of houses for all sections of society, the first urban area 
specific housing policy—the National Urban Housing & Habitat Policy (NUHHP), 2007 has been 
formulated, which has been laid on the Table of both Houses of the Parliament on 7.12.2007. The Policy 
seeks to set in motion a process forproviding "Affordable Housing for All" particularly for Economically 
Weaker Sections (EWS) and Low Income Groups (LIG) t hrough various types of public-private 
partnerships and development of various financial and operational innovations. 
Apart from NUHHP, 2007, the Jawaharlal Nehru Nation al Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) 
launched by the Government in the year 2005 caters for provisions of housing and basic services to 
urban poor in 63 specified cities and also for non-specified cities. Also a provision of Rs. 30 crores has 
been made in the current financial year 2007-08 to provide housing for provide interest rate subsidy 
scheme for loans to Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Low Income Groups (LIG). 
A Task Force has also been set up by this Ministry to look into various aspects of providing 
"Affordable Housing for AH" and recommend ways and means of enhancing accessibility of 
EWS/LIG groups to housing with suitable governmental support and recommend ways and means of 
enhancing accessibility of MIG groups to housing ap art from developing innovative financial 
instruments for bringing flexibility in the housing  market and making recommendations as to fiscal, 
spatial incentives for increasing supply of houses.

ARC Recommendations for urban poor 
271. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the Minister of  HOU SING AND URBAN POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether it is a fact that the Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) has recommended for 
conducting a survey to identify urban poor in the country; 
(b)  if so, the details of the recommendations; and 
(c)  the other recommendations made by the Commission with regard to urban poor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AN D URBAN POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. T he Second Administrative Reforms 
Commission (ARC), in its Sixth Report concerning Lo cal Governance has recommended that "an 
exhaustive survey to identify the urban poor should be carried out within one year. 

Written Answers to  [28 FEB. 2008]  Unstarred Questions   83 
The parameters to be used for such identification s hould be simple and easily comprehensible, 
allowing objective measurement without the use of discretion. The identification should be based on a 
door-to-door survey with the survey teams including  at least one person form the Area Sabha 
concerned. The urban poor so identified may be issued multi-utility identity cards for availing benefits 
under all poverty alleviation programmes." 
(c) Other major recommendations of the Commission with regard to urban poverty are: 
(i) After identifying the urban poor through survey s, a mission mode approach would need 
to be adopted for alleviating urban poverty in a time-bound and systematic manner. The 
urban local bodies may also have their own poverty alleviation schemes with adequate 
background and forward linkages converging with the other poverty alleviation schemes. 
00 The thrust of the urban poverty alleviation schemes should be on upgradation of skills and 
training. 
(iii) In case of setting up of micro-enterprises, the urban poverty alleviation schemes should be 
flexible in selecting projects and providing financial assistance. 
(iv) To maximize the benefits of micro-finance, formation of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) need to be 
encouraged. Institutions and NGOs with good track r ecord should be encouraged to 
promote SHGs for availing micro-finance. 
(v) The education plan should form an integral part of the development plan for the city. 
(vi) Urban Local Bodies should adopt the concept of'Primary Health Care' for providing health 
and medical facilities to the urban poor, particula rly to women and children with the 
help of auxiliary staff. These should specifically cater to the population living in slum 
areas. 
(vii) There has to be total redevelopment of slum a reas. While redeveloping, it should be 
ensured that adequate provision has been made for s chools, health centre, sanitation 
etc. 
(viii) It is necessary to earmark and reserve a cer tain percentage of land in housing projects in 
each town and city for the urban poor. If a construction cannot allocate housing for the poor, 
the developer must, at his own cost, provide suitab le housing in any other appropriate 
place acceptable to the authorities. 
(ix) A detailed programme for the provision of night shelters needs to be drawn up in all cities, 
beginning with large cities having Metropolitan and  Municipal Corporations, for 
implementation.

(b)  if so, the details including the number of above ci tizens for the-last five years, State-wise, 
category-wise, year-wise and family-wise; 
(c)  if so, the number of people below poverty line for the last five years, year-wise and State-wise; 
 (d) if so, the criteria adopted to determine the poverty line as on today; and 
(e) if so, whether the Competent Authority would in itiate step to evolve new criteria for

 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI M.V. 
RAJASEKHARAN): (a) Based on the percentage of rural and urban population below specified levels of 
monthly per capita concumption expenditure (MPCE) given in the Report No. 508 (61 /1.01), 'Level and 
Pattern of Consumer Expenditure, 2004-05', of NSS 61 st Round (July 2004-June 2005) brought out by the 
National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, 
Government of India, the per capita consumption expenditure of 60.5% of the population is less than Rs.

88    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
(b)  The State-wise percentage of persons with per capit a consumption expenditure of Rs. 20 per 
day in rural and urban areas in 2004-05 estimated f rom the National Sample Survey (NSS) data on 
consumer expenditure, relating to the 61 st Round i s given in the Statement-1 (See below). Large 
sample survey data on consumer expenditure are available once in approximately five years. As such, 
the estimates for each of the last five years are not available. Such information at the level of fami lies 
are not available. 
(c)  The Planning Commission estimates poverty at the Na tional and State level from the large 
sample survey on household consumer expenditure con ducted by the National Sample Survey 
Organization (NSSO) at an interval of approximately  five years following the methodology 
contained in the report of the Expert Group on Esti mation of Proportion and Number of Poor 
(Lakdawala Committee). The latest estimate of pover ty is available for year 2004-05. As such, the 
poverty estimates for each of the last five years are not available. The two latest comparable estimat e 
of poverty are available for the years 1993-94 and 2004-05 estimated from the large sample survey 
data on household consumer expenditure o. the 50th and 61st Rounds of NSS respectively. The State-wise 
estimates of the number of poor in 1993-94 and 2004-05 are given in the Statement-II and Statement-Ill 
respectively (See below). 
(d)  The Planning Commission uses a poverty line based on per capita consumption expenditure as 
the criterion to determine the persons living below  the poverty line. The poverty line is expressed in  
terms of per capita consumption expenditure needed to attain a minimum amount of calorie intake out of 
food consumption along with a minimum amount of non -food expenditure in order to meet the 
requirements of clothing, shelter, transport etc. T he per capita consumption norm has been fixed at Rs. 
49.09 per month in rural areas and Rs. 56.64 per month in urban areas at 1973-74 prices at national level 
corresponding to a basket of goods and services anchored on a norm of per capita daily calorie requirement 
of 2400 kcal in rural areas and 2100 kcal in urban areas. The State-specific poverty lines are derived 
from the national level poverty lines, using State-specific price indices and inter-state price differentials. 
The national poverty line at 2004-05 prices is Rs. 356 per capital per month in the rural areas and Rs . 
538.60 per capita per month in the urban areas. 
(e)  There is no such proposal, at the moment.

Programme for poor population 
278. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a)  the current population of the country, rural and urban separately; 
(b)  the number of poor and the rich out of the above; 
(c)  the housing, employment opportunities and disbursement of food items planned and 
implemented for the poor, both rural and urban, during the last three years; 
(d)  whether no data of the poor has been complied for the last three years; and 
(e)  if so, the reasons therefor and the basis and manner in which plans are made, imple-
mented and funds earmarked and expended on various programmes for the poor during the 
last three years? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING ( SHRI M.V. 
RAJASEKHARAN): (a) As per the Report of Technical G roup on Population Projections 
constituted by the National Commission on Population entitled, 'Population Projections for 

Written Answers to  [28 FEB. 2008]  Unstarred Questions   93 
India and States 2001-2026' brought out by the Offi ce of Registrar General and Census 
Commissioner, India, the population of the country as on 1st March, 2008 is projected as 
1144.7 million, with 335.9 million of urban population and 808.8 million of rural population. 
(b) The Planning Commission estimates the incidence  of poverty in the rural and 
urban areas of the country from the large sample su rvey on household consumer 
expenditure conducted by the National Sample Survey  Organisation (NSSO) at an 
interval of approximately five years following the methodology contained in the report 
   of the Expert Group on Estimation of Proportion and Number of Poor (Lakdawala 
Committee). The latest estimate of the incidence of poverty is available for the year 
 2004-05, based on the large sample survey data on household consumer expenditure 
conducted by the NSSO in its 61st Round (July 2004- June 2005). As such, it is not 
possible to decompose the current population (2008)  into poor and non-poor. Based 
 on the latest estimate of poverty, the number of poor in 2004-05 is estimated as 301.7 
million, with 220.9 million in the rural areas and 80.8 million in the urban areas. Accord-
ingly, in 2004-05,795.4 million people are non-poor  with 559.8 million in the rural areas 
and 233.6 million in the urban areas. The informati on on the number of rich is not 
available. 
(c) Addressing housing shortage is an important str ategy of poverty alleviation in 
India. Under Bharat Nirman, Rural Housing is one of  the six components. During 
2007-08, an amount of Rs. 4040 crore has been alloc ated for Rural Housing with the 
target of 21.27 lakh houses under the Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY). Allocation of plan 
funds to Ministry of Housing and Poverty Alleviatio n which is responsible for Housing 
and Poverty Alleviation programmes for urban poor during 2005-06,2006-07 and 2007-08 
was Rs. 499.51 crore, Rs. 421.67 crore & Rs 500 cro re respectively. As per the two most 
recent quinquennial rounds of National Sample Surve y Organisation in (NSSO) on 
Employment and Unemployment Surveys, employment opp ortunities (for rural and ur 
ban areas combined) on current Daily Status basis i ncreased from 338.19 million in 1999- 
2000 (55th Round) to 384.91 million in 2004-05 (61s t Round). For Rural Employment, 
various programmes are being implemented viz. Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana 
(SGSY), Sampoorma Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY), National Rural Employment Guar 
antee Programme (NREGP). The Financial and physical performance under SGSY, SGRY 
and IAY is given in the Statement I (See below). A Statement showing the Total Alloca 
tion and Offtake of Foodgrains (wheat and rice) und er Targeted Public Distribution 
System and Other Welfare Schemes as well as total Offtake under below poverty line 
 (BPL) and Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) for the year 2004-05, 2005-06 and 2006-07 is 
given in Statement -II [See below). 
(d) and (e) The estimates of poverty are made from the large sample survey data on 
            consumer expenditure which are obtained from the National Sample Survey Organisation 
(NSSO) at an interval of approximately five years. The latest estimate of poverty is avail-
able for the year 2004-05 estimated from the NSS co nsumer expenditure data of the 61st 
Round. Plan are based on estimate of poverty comput ed from the quinquennial survey of 
consumer expenditure of the NSSO. These estimates a re integrated into the planning 
system by the application of analytical methods. The anti-poverty programmes and schemes 
are formulated on the basis of the assessed needs made by the concerned Ministries.

RAJASEKHARAN): (a) In the electricity, fuels and gas sectors, the grants-in-aid by the Government 
to the Central Electricity Regulatory Authority (CERC) were Rs. 5.84 crore in 2005-06 and Rs. 5.65 
crore in 2006-07, while no expenditures were incurr ed in respect of the Joint Electricity Regulatory

2.0 crore in 2005-06 and Rs. 2.86 crore in 2006-07.

Commission it has been observed that the regulatory  framework that has emerged in the 
infrastructure sectors over the last fifteen years is characterized by the establishment of independen t 
regulatory commissions on a sectoral basis, and rec ommends that consideration should be given to 
establishing multi-sectoral regualtors for (a) comm unications, (b) electricity, fuels and gas, and (c)

expertise, promote consistency of approach and save on costs. It recommends that the States should

(a) and (b) Meetings at high levels including the Group of Ministers, Lt. Governor, GNCTD, Cabinet Secretariat etc. 
are regularly held to assess prearation for the Commonwealth Games. Action Taken Reports on decisions taken in 
such meetings are reviewed during the course of the next meeting to ensure that required actions have been

(c) Government are conscious of the need to ensure proper planning and timely preparation for the

include a Core Group of Ministers (GoM) under the co-Chairmanship of the Minister for Human Resource 
Development and the Home Minister for coordinating the various works related to the conduct of the Games; an apex 
Committee headed by the Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports to oversee preparations; an Organizing Committee 
(OC) headed by the President, Indian Olympic Association for the Conduct of the Games; and a Committee of 
Secretaries headed by Cabinet Secretary which is responsible for monitoring the implementation of the 
decisions of the GoM and taking decisions on other related matters. In addition to these arrangements at the 
Central level, there is a sub-committee under the Chief Minister of Delhi to take decisions in respect of all 
matters pertaining to infrastructure and other preparations for the Games within the jurisdiction of the 
Government of NCT of Delhi. The Lt. Governor Delhi has been entrusted with the overall responsibility for matters 
comming under DDA and with specific reference to security, law and order. An Empowered Committee has 
been set up under the chairmanship of Chief secretary, GNCTD, with representatives from all the agencies/ 
authorities concerned to facilitate speedy clearances in respect of Games-related projects. Another Committee 
has been set up Under Secretary, Ministry of Urban Development to facilitate clearances pertaining to the Delhi 
Urban Arts Commission (DUAC). Keeping in view the need for developing adequate tourist accommodation in 
readiness for the large expected influx of visitors for the Commonwealth Games, an inter-Ministerial Task Force 
has been set up under the Ministry of Tourism (MoT) for monitoring and coordinating further action in this 
regard by all the agencies concerned. A Committee for expediting Central Government clearances in respect of 
hotels coming up in Uttar Pradesh has also been set up under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of 
Youth Affairs and Sports.

regularisation of construction already existing as on 22.9.2006 on payment of charges as per

Written Answers to  [28 FEB. 2008]  Unstarred Questions    121 
Regularization of unauthorized colonies  
+311. DR. PRABHATHAK.UR: Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether thousands of people are living in many unathorised colonies of Delhi; 
(b)  the number of unauthorised colonies not regularised as yet by Government in Delhi and the 
reasons therefor: 
(c)  whether Government has formulated any plan regardin g regularisation of such unauthorised 
colonies; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and whether any order ha s been issued for the regularisation of 
colonies, the names of the colonies and by when; 
(e)  whether any scheme has been formulated in this regard and its details thereof; and 
(f)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVE LOPMENT (SHRI 
AJAY MAKEN): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) to (f) The Central Government has decided to re gularize unauthorized colonies (except those 
inhabited by affluent sections of society). Detaile d guidelines in this regard have been issued on 
5.10.2007. The guidelines inter alia contain general principles, recovery of cost of land, registration 
of residents' society, steps for regularization, et c. Government of NCT of Delhi (GNCTD) has 
forwarded list containing the names of unauthorized colonies which have applied for regularization in 
response to the public notice issued by the GNCTD. Those colonies which fulfil the conditions laid 
down in the guidelines shall be eligible for regula rization. Clause 4.2 (i) of revised guidelines 2007 
issued by the Government of India on 5th October, 2 007 stipulate that after the receipt of the 
applications for regularization. the entire process  of regularization of colony by GNCTD except 
change in land use is to be completed within six mo nths and formal regularization after effecting 
change in land use within 9 months. In case the time limit prescribed above needs relaxation in respect 
of some colonies, the Lt. Governor, Delhi may relax the time limit on specific request of GNCTD. 
However, as per clause 5.4 of the revised guideline s, 2007, GNCTD may commence the 
development works and augmentation of infrastructure facilities in public interest in colonies/ part of 
colonies soon after the receipt of layout plan, if it is satisfied that these colonies or parts thereo f 
fulfil the general principles contained in these guidelines. 
As per Clause 4.1 of the revised guidelines 2007 'H abitations'existing as on 31.3.2002 that have 
come up as extension to village abadi and have not been notified as Lal Dora extension to village abadi 
would be eligible for regi. ianzation on the same lines as unauthorized colonies subject to meeting the 
requirements of Regulations framed pursuant to these guidelines. 
Final regularization has to take into account applicable orders of Hon'ble Supreme Court and High 
Court of Delhi.
